neighbours.label: A hedge or qualifier that closes a claim: ' so' as a pro-form after a degree word ('but not extremely so', 'desperately so', 'more so'), 'or so it seemed', 'at least' at the end; ' so' as a conjunction or before an adjective, and 'at least' before a number, stay quiet.
fire: The fever is dangerous, though not terribly so.
She was angry, and rightly so.
The road seems safe, or so we were told.
It is popular in Texas at least.
Their plan is risky, perhaps needlessly so.
The soup tasted sweet, more so than usual.
He is honest, or so it appeared.
It is cheap here at least.
quiet: The fever is dangerous, so call a doctor.
She was so angry at the bank.
The road seems safe, so we went on.
It is popular with at least six people in Texas.
Their plan is so risky that I left.
The soup tasted sweet, and I was glad.
He is honest, and I trust him.
It is cheap in at least two shops here.

short: hedge closing a claim ('not extremely so')
notes: Probes: ' so' 0.78-1.10, ' seemed' 0.75, ' least' 0.35. Conjunction and adjective ' so' under 0.01, 'At least ten' 0.01. 'by the most conservative reckoning' 0.85 and 'only as old as you feel' 0.85 fit a qualifier loosely, and they are not tested.
